cases.contract: Official created CHK parsed by Rust and Rust output parsed by official implementation, including zero and maximal file lengths.
Alias/padding/case handling and canonical output preserve all hash bytes.
Missing/truncated hash, separator, size, embedded NUL and capacity rejection cannot expose a partial artifact.
C and Rust cross-parse empty, slash-bearing and percent-bearing identifiers.
Opaque non-UTF8 bytes preserve identity where the public string boundary can represent them.
Malformed keys or caller resource limits reject without writes.
Cross-parse optional/mandatory terms, duplicate and literal plus payloads.
Official constructor marker-only %2B remains one mandatory term with zero payload.
Malformed escapes and unbalanced syntax reject safely.
Keep the three observed C-permissive optional-empty/raw-quote differences explicit; do not call every C input accepted.
C-created/Rust-created LOCs authenticate in the other implementation.
Every changed signed field and signature is rejected.
Whole-second creation and nonwhole wrapped authenticated input cannot silently serialize an invalid signature.
Expired authentic artifact stays distinguishable from a consumer availability/expiration decision.
Cross-implementation plaintext/key/query/ciphertext/MAC equivalence at zero, one byte, 32767/32768 bytes.
Wrong query, key, ciphertext or tag never releases authenticated plaintext.
Short output/scratch fails atomically with no input/state loss.
A public primitive composition oracle is labeled primitive-only, not original complete FS encoder verification.
Empty file and 32768 boundary produce the same root CHK and file size as original FS.
256 leaves, 256 leaves plus one byte, multi-index levels and partial final nodes match official encoding.
Large-size/u64 overflow paths remain bounded and never wrap indexing/offset arithmetic.
Decode exact plaintext size and tree shape; reject missing/extra/wrong child bytes in file context.
No new type-AAD or magic is invented; raw valid bytes may admit multiple contextual interpretations.
C compressed and uncompressed v2 metadata parses in Rust and Rust-produced metadata parses in C.
UTF8/C-string/binary values and null/empty metadata retain meaning.
Entry sizes, unsupported versions, unterminated strings, decompression failure and output limits are bounded.
Partial serialization policy preserves legal selected entries without claiming all entries were retained.
Distinguish strict malformed-input refusal from C partial-container recovery; record actual differences.
C and Rust full/partial directory parse and construction cross-check entry URIs, metadata, names and embedded data.
Cross a 32KiB block boundary, padding, directory metadata, empty directory and recursive directories.
Truncated URI/length/metadata yields explicit incomplete/error status without OOB reads.
KSK entries reject; inline bytes must match contextual CHK and declared file size.
Untrusted names and extraction targets cannot overwrite unrelated paths; product path policy is explicit.
Cross-construct and authenticate keyword and signed namespace UBLOCKs including update identifier.
Derive query from verification key and reject wrong namespace/label/signature/purpose/size.
Verify MAC before interpreting strings or metadata; malformed plaintext cannot become a search result.
Maximum legal blocks, metadata truncation, empty update marker and expired publication policy are exercised.
Compare official word/quote/mandatory handling against Rust UI input.
Metadata lowercase+NFD behavior, invalid UTF8/locale conversion and short-token policy are version/profile bound.
Merging optional/mandatory duplicates preserves intended mandatory satisfaction.
Artifact term byte preservation is not mislabeled metadata normalization or query execution.
Publish equivalent bytes from file, memory and incremental reader to equal CHK output.
Nested empty/nonempty directories retain links, entry metadata and options.
Reader errors, changed/truncated source, cancellation and resource exhaustion produce explicit failure.
Independent concurrent publications retain distinct sources and progress.
Rust publisher content is downloadable by official nodes and official publication is downloadable by Rust.
Full insertion and on-demand index modes both work for files and directories.
Simulate-only calculates artifacts without committing datastore/network state.
Cancellation/error cannot report completed publication or replay a stale operation.
Bounded retries and dependency loss preserve independent operations and the selected anonymity policy.
Official search finds Rust keyword publication and Rust finds official keyword publication.
Mandatory/optional keyword selection and metadata-derived variants bind the intended exact labels.
Partial failure/cancel does not report all mappings successful; no stale continuation is reused.
Cross-node lookup finds signed namespace records and follows next-version identifiers.
Different namespaces and identical labels never alias authority.
Update graph roots, branches, cycles and duplicate discoveries stay bounded and preserve required discoverability.
Failure, cancellation and restart cannot fabricate a locally published update.
Official client indexes through Rust service and Rust client indexes through official service.
Valid file gets exact success; changed content, unreadable path, or mismatched hash gets failure with valid terminated reason.
Reserved/filename/frame errors are refused safely; fragmentation and back-to-back frames retain original requests.
Cancellation/EOF while hashing retires original source and suppresses stale completion.
Both client/service directions compare empty, one and multiple entries plus end marker.
Long/opaque filenames and exact hash values survive framing.
Missing terminator, malformed entry, EOF before END and cancel never imply a complete list.
Cross-direction existing/absent unindex acknowledgement matches service behavior.
After unindex, content no longer obtains an on-demand source from the removed file; unrelated indexed sources survive.
Partial transport, cancel, file removal and restart cannot produce duplicate or foreign completion.
An official datastore on-demand record is resolved by Rust FS and produces the original expected encrypted block.
Offset/tail, missing/modified file, invalid offset and stale index state never return unrelated bytes.
Rust-native storage may use a different private record format only in a profile that does not expose official type6 records.
Official publishing client accepts valid Rust service LOC and Rust client verifies official service reply.
Non-palindromic u64 file length catches endian mistakes; rounded time and identity must authenticate.
Wrong purpose/claim/key/time, partial reply/EOF/cancel and identity replacement cannot complete the original request.
Both IPC directions handle complete and fragmented already-seen lists beyond one frame.
Distinct concurrent query/type/target requests do not merge, including continuation and duplicate request cases.
Loopback-only never initiates P2P; anonymous requests do not leak targeted direct lookup behavior.
EOF/cancel/reconnect retain original request ownership and known-result suppression without stale callbacks.
Both client directions parse real result metadata and exact encrypted payload without confusing peer layout.
DBLOCK/IBLOCK single completion and UBLOCK multiple results/duplicates obey their contracts.
Wrong query/type/signature/MAC/expiration and malformed plaintext never become successful results.
Out-of-order concurrent results, canceled requests and old physical connections cannot settle another request.
Cross-node AND semantics hide a result until all required keywords are satisfied.
Optional support/duplicate arrivals cannot invent extra results or decrement a missing requirement twice.
Result URI and metadata retain identity across independent keyword subqueries.
Pause/continue and reconnect preserve delivered-result suppression and allow genuinely new results.
Rust and official peers discover both initial signed results and next-version entries.
Wrong namespace/identifier/signature fails even when URI/metadata parses.
Cyclic/branching updates, duplicate URIs and stopping parent searches retain bounded independent ownership.
Available and unavailable search results produce truthful updates from actual transfer activity.
Stop probe, parent search cancellation and restarted physical connection cannot issue stale updates.
Probes never persist as normal downloads and do not bypass anonymity or resource budgets.
Download official publication with Rust and Rust publication with official clients using CHK and LOC.
Empty/full/tail/range and >8MiB multi-level content reconstruct exact logical bytes.
Corrupt/mismatched/missing block and bad LOC authority cannot report completion.
File/callback output, optional temporaries and reuse of existing partial file data retain verified offsets.
Mixed-node nested directory and inline files produce expected byte trees and metadata.
Search stop does not incorrectly abort an associated download; parent loss yields explicit ownership transition.
Untrusted entry names, duplicate paths, recursion limits, partial directory data and cancellation do not corrupt unrelated outputs.
Cancel before send, after partial write, before reply and during dependency failure terminates the correct original operation.
Completed/error remain distinct and observed terminal effects occur at most once.
Concurrent operations and resource refusal preserve healthy independent work.
Pause/continue, suspend/resume and explicit stop have distinct durable and callback consequences.
No callback is delivered after a completed global stop; caller reentrancy is specified without copying C pointer ABI.
Restart each supported operation after actual progress and observe resume without false completion or wrong ownership.
Retain known search results, child associations, verified download ranges and namespace update graph.
Interrupted/corrupt/missing state and failed storage commits reject or recover explicitly; never activate unverified data.
Canceled/deleted operations stay retired after restart; independently healthy state survives another corrupt record.
Private Rust store format changes require own-state correctness, not old Rust/C on-disk migration.
C-to-Rust and Rust-to-C CORE request frames match query and optional return/transmit targets.
All supported bitmap combinations and Bloom boundaries parse with checked lengths; unknown/unsupported flags have reviewed policy.
Milliseconds remain distinct from microsecond local clocks; extreme signed TTL and decrement cannot overflow.
Missing reverse route, queue refusal, stale peer and cancellation cannot route a reply to a foreign owner.
Both peer directions deliver valid data/index/universal blocks and expected expiry.
Changed payload/key/signature/query/type rejects; unsolicited results cannot satisfy an unrelated pending request.
Multiple requesters, duplicate replies and one-shot data results preserve completion and suppression.
Mixed multi-hop C/Rust topologies exercise both origin directions and transit roles.
Loopback-only stays local; anonymity>0 does not silently downgrade to direct targeted CADET/DHT access.
Repeated requests/loops, expired TTL, Bloom known results and overload remain bounded and avoid false positives.
Peer disconnect/reconnect retires reverse routes and original outstanding work without replay on replacement ownership.
Rust resource policy may differ, but cannot invent replies or violate exposed anonymity guarantees.
Both directions accept valid pushed content and explicit migration-stop duration.
While blocked the target receives no new migration; expiry re-enables legal pushing without duplicate timer ownership.
Queue/dependency failure and repeated stop/clock changes preserve bounds and distinguish local send from remote storage.
Replication and expiration policy changes remain externally meaningful without copying C selection order.
C server/Rust client and Rust server/C client transfer actual content and reject wrong hash/type/MAC.
Concurrent queries and partial reply/EOF/cancel cannot deliver another channel/request result.
Channel capacity, reset/reconnect and idle close remain bounded with truthful error outcomes.
CADET profile success is separate from anonymous CORE routing and complete FS acceptance.
Service unavailable, identity change, datastore full and dependency EOF preserve original operations and distinct errors.
Clock rollback/refusal, disconnect/restart and late replies cannot activate a new identity from old capability.
Mixed official service profiles verify every actually exposed IPC boundary; direct Rust assembly need not emulate unused C API/plugin loader.
Declared supported platform profiles instantiate real endpoint ACL/path/port and filesystem semantics.
Configured admission bounds reject locally/explicitly without corrupting unrelated active operations.
Maximum frames, slow writers, partial I/O, termination and unsupported options keep finite resource ownership.
Measure performance/RAM/stack separately from compile-only M0/M4 and functional evidence.
Equivalent local directory input yields expected publish tree and metadata/keywords, including extractor-disabled mode.
Unreadable files, symlinks/platform variants, abort and extractor failure produce meaningful bounded outcomes.
Raw full paths are not published unintentionally; original filename and supported media metadata policy are explicit.
If selected, cross-parse progress file/directory, skip/error, counting-done, metadata and finished notifications.
Filename NUL, traversal marker, metadata/current-entry association and empty completion payloads are checked.
Partial frame, helper EOF/exit/error, abort and repeated terminal notification never become successful scan.
If replaced by Rust-native extraction, retain explicit reviewed profile N/A rationale while keeping all seven registry identities in the floor.
Publish from files/URI/namespace with noindex/simulate/metadata/keyword/replication/priority/anonymity controls.
Search bookmark-only/local/timeout/result-count/output-directory and supported formatting semantics work.
Download local/recursive/output/concurrency/delete-incomplete choices work on real transfer.
Auto-share observes local updates and persists/republishes truthfully without fake successful uploads.
Argument errors and interruption have explicit outcomes; exact gettext phrasing/help columns are not an implicit protocol prerequisite.

operations.contract: Exact scheme/type, two SHA-512 values in key/query order and u64 length; standard normalization and explicit bounded malformed-input behavior.
operations.title: CHK public content identifier

operations.contract: Namespace EdDSA key plus literal identifier remainder; no DNS/path/percent interpretation.
operations.title: SKS public namespace identifier

operations.contract: Encoded term order, duplicates, mandatory marker and balanced quote syntax are data artifacts, separate from UI tokenization and set operations.
operations.title: KSK public keyword artifact

operations.contract: Exact purpose5 placement signature binds content, file length, peer and expiration; artifact authenticity is separate from current validity/storage/reachability.
operations.title: Authenticated LOC placement artifact

operations.contract: SHA512 plaintext forms CHK key; GNUnet HKDF labels derive XChaCha20Poly1305 material; empty AAD, detached MAC appended; query hashes complete ciphertext plus MAC.
operations.title: DBLOCK/IBLOCK cryptographic byte artifacts

operations.contract: 32KiB leaf plaintext, 256 children per index, each CHK key64/query64. Derive depth and exact tail geometry from total file size, supporting all representable practical sizes rather than only the first 8MiB.
operations.title: Complete CHK tree and file reconstruction

operations.contract: Header/entry framing, compressed flag, typed values, MIME/plugin names and null representation must interoperate. Compression algorithm implementation and metadata container layout may differ.
operations.title: Serialized metadata v2 and value semantics

operations.contract: Directory magic/header metadata plus NUL URI, metadata-length and metadata entries with 32KiB alignment and optional full-data metadata; KSK cannot be a file entry.
operations.title: GNUnet directory and inline-file artifacts

operations.contract: Purpose-prefixed derived EdDSA signature and verification key cover encrypted update identifier, URI, metadata and MAC; derive with fs-ublock and UBLOCK-ENC labels, then exact content key derivation.
operations.title: Keyword/namespace universal result block

operations.contract: UI words, mandatory flags, metadata-derived keywords, duplicate merge and Unicode normalization that selects exact lookup keys must be explicit separate capabilities.
operations.title: Search/publication keyword construction

operations.contract: Users can publish explicit bytes, files, readers and nested directories with metadata, keywords and publication options; source ownership and cancellation must remain safe.
operations.title: File/directory publication inputs

operations.contract: Store encoded data/index blocks and associated results with expiration, priority, anonymity and replication policy; simulate-only must not publish.
operations.title: File/directory publication and insertion/index modes

operations.contract: Publish each selected keyword mapping with the anonymous namespace key and exact derived lookup key, result URI and metadata.
operations.title: Keyword publication

operations.contract: Publish chosen identifier and optional next-version identifier using the selected namespace identity, and preserve updateable graph behavior.
operations.title: Signed namespace publication and update discovery

operations.contract: FS_INDEX_START packed fields bind filename and full plaintext file hash; missing/mismatching file rejects. Device/inode matching is an optional safe optimization, not a required Rust mechanism.
operations.title: Index request and acceptance

operations.contract: FS_INDEX_LIST_GET yields entry hash/filename records then FS_INDEX_LIST_END, with caller cancellation/EOF behavior.
operations.title: Indexed-file list and termination

operations.contract: FS_UNINDEX identifies plaintext file hash and replies FS_UNINDEX_OK even when absent; product unindex additionally retires local on-demand references and related state.
operations.title: Unindex request and acknowledgement

operations.contract: Where the official datastore boundary is used, type6 records carry full-file hash and NBO offset; resolve the currently validated plaintext source and encode the requested block.
operations.title: On-demand indexed block resolution

operations.contract: FS_REQUEST_LOC_SIGN/FS_REQUEST_LOC_SIGNATURE exchange exact purpose, file claim, actual peer identity and rounded expiration; verify the service reply against the original request.
operations.title: Service placement-signing request/response

operations.contract: FS_START_SEARCH identifies block type, anonymity, optional target, query and already-seen result hashes; continuation fragments retain intended query/type/target and start exactly once.
operations.title: FS search request, continuation and cancellation

operations.contract: Client FS_PUT has a distinct 32-byte prefix including transfer observations; peer FS_PUT uses a 16-byte prefix. Validate block type/key/query/signature before exposing content.
operations.title: FS result delivery and validation

operations.contract: Derived keyword queries, all mandatory terms, optional support, result deduplication and metadata aggregation determine observable search results.
operations.title: Mandatory/optional keyword search aggregation

operations.contract: Authenticate and decrypt SKS results under the original namespace/identifier, discover associated next-version searches, and bound cycles.
operations.title: Namespace search and update chains

operations.contract: Optional probes measure availability and emit typed updates without claiming permanent storage, while respecting selected anonymity and owner priority.
operations.title: Search availability probes and updates

operations.contract: Resolve the content tree, verify/decrypt before delivery, and return exact logical file bytes; a requested range is a focus hint at block granularity, not a promise against surrounding block writes.
operations.title: CHK/LOC transfer and focused ranges

operations.contract: Download directory metadata/entries/inline files and attach child downloads; detaching a stopped search preserves a live associated download as standalone.

source_refs.anchor: Download parts of a file based on a search result.

operations.title: Directory recursion and associated downloads

operations.contract: Provide meaningful start/progress/error/completed/stop, pause/continue/suspend/resume and cancellation ownership as appropriate. Rust enums/callback API may differ; no post-stop notification or false success.
operations.title: Observable publication/search/download/unindex lifecycle

operations.contract: Requested persistence restores publication/search/results/download/unindex and updateable namespace progress, preserving verified content and observable associations; Rust disk encoding need not equal private C BIO records.
operations.title: Persistent operation and namespace recovery

operations.contract: Exact type/priority/signed millisecond TTL/reserved/bitmap/query and ordered optional peer identities plus reply-suppression Bloom data; address hash comment must not substitute 32-byte peer identities.
operations.title: Anonymous CORE FS_GET request

operations.contract: Peer result has type, expiration and encrypted payload; validate/extract the exact block query before delivering/routing, preserving duplicate and type-specific terminal semantics.
operations.title: CORE FS_PUT response and block routing

operations.contract: Implement required anonymous and nonanonymous retrieval, reverse routing, bounded request lifetime, duplicate suppression, priorities and cover-traffic policy without copying C scheduler/queue/scoring internals.
operations.title: Forwarding, suppression, anonymity and load behavior

operations.contract: Support unsolicited content where configured, cache/replication effects and FS_MIGRATION_STOP duration semantics; no peer retention guarantee is inferred from a local send.
operations.title: Content caching, pushing and migration suppression

operations.contract: Use the official hashed fs-block port, query72-byte type+query frame, reply16-byte type+expiration frame plus encoded DBLOCK/IBLOCK; match the requested hash/type and original channel.
operations.title: Nonanonymous fs-block CADET transfer

operations.contract: Own actual peer identity/signing and required datastore/BLOCK/CORE/CADET/discovery/peer credit operations behind typed Rust ports or independently compatible service clients; no production C FFI substitutes ownership.
operations.title: FS service identity, datastore and shared dependencies

operations.contract: Expose required local/remote service accessibility and selected behavior settings, bounded active requests/downloads/CADET clients/storage queues and clean shutdown; internal allocator/runtime may differ.
operations.title: Bounded FS host and supported platform configuration

operations.contract: Read local files/directories with explicit extraction policy, progress/skip/error, safe original filenames, keyword derivation and abort. Rust may invoke a typed extractor or perform equivalent extraction in process.
operations.title: Directory scanning and metadata extraction user capability

operations.condition: Only required if the Rust product chooses to communicate with or expose the official publish-helper process boundary. Metadata scanning/extraction remains required independently.
operations.contract: Seven registered helper-to-client notifications are a real framed boundary if Rust chooses to communicate with the official helper; preserving the feature does not mandate this process separation.
operations.title: Official publish-helper interoperation profile

operations.contract: Provide publish/search/download/directory-inspection/index-list/unindex/auto-share capabilities and their substantive flags; Rust API/CLI layout and human help formatting may differ unless a separate CLI compatibility promise is selected.
operations.title: Complete FS user operations and CLI-facing capabilities

Actual original FS file/tree artifacts in both directions; primitive-only KDF/AEAD oracle is insufficient for complete tree
Derived signature, label/query, AEAD and result URI/metadata
User/metadata query words and normalized exact lookup labels
Official client to Rust service plus Rust client to official service; same original physical connection and cancellation identity
Multi-hop FS anonymous CORE request/result/transit/migration with real block data
Official fs-block CADET application and real directed data transfer
Data/index store effects and shared file downloadability
Keyword publications and AND/optional/dedup search results
Official datastore FS_ONDEMAND record boundary if selected
Actual bounded probe observations and cancellation

Substantive user operations and supported configuration/platform semantics

registry_classifications.proposed_boundary: Two role-specific layouts: CORE peer and FS local IPC

scope: Source-bound draft only. Every case/profile/direction, owner scope and source interpretation still requires independent semantic review and actual evidence. Optional helper IPC does not mandate a C process/ABI; the scanning feature remains required. Counts are draft review units, not a permanent C-helper floor. Conditional helper IPC may be classified nonselected only by a later independently reviewed architecture/boundary determination that preserves required metadata extraction; no draft status or unsupported claim resolves unknowns.
